title: Claude Code memory: CLAUDE.md and auto memory
by: Anthropic's Claude Code docs, page 'How Claude remembers your project'. Read in full.
summary: Claude Code carries knowledge across sessions in two ways: CLAUDE.md files that people write, and auto memory that Claude writes itself. Both load at session start as context, not enforced configuration; anything that must happen every time belongs in a hook. Auto memory keeps one file per memory and a short MEMORY.md index, of which only the first 200 lines or 25KB load.
ideas: CLAUDE.md loads from the working directory and every directory above it; files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude touches a file there; .claude/rules/ files with a paths field load only for matching files.
@path imports pull other files in, up to four hops deep, but they still cost context; aim for under 200 lines per file.
If two instructions contradict, Claude may follow either; there is no precedence between a user rule and a project rule, so remove conflicts (/doctor prompt-audit finds them).
Auto memory has four types, user, feedback, project and reference, stored in frontmatter; Claude skips anything it can derive from the code or that CLAUDE.md already says.
MEMORY.md is an index, one line per memory; near the 200-line or 25KB limit Claude Code tells Claude to shorten it, and over the limit it returns an error asking for a rewrite.
Claude Code stamps a 'modified' ISO time into a memory's frontmatter on each write, so a reader can tell how current a fact is.
Memory is advisory: to block or force an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a hook such as PreToolUse.

took.idea: A short index loaded at start, one line per thing that holds, with the docs read on demand
Enforce the write path with a hook, since instructions alone are advisory
Do not store what can be derived; compute it
The tool, not the agent, stamps the time and author of each write
A size budget on what loads at start, with a warning near it and an error past it
